dedupe_keys.name: aperta path first cross modal accessibility analysis library

description: Aperta is an open-source Python library for cross-modal accessibility analysis on transport networks. Its path-first routing returns the realised route together with the travel cost as a single primitive; a tiered origin-destination structure keeps the computation tractable from city to country scale; and mode and network are independent, so walking, cycling and car accessibility computed on different networks combine directly. It also includes traffic flow estimation and iterative calibration of edge weights. It is generic and works on any network in any country. Releases are archived on Zenodo with DOIs, the latest being version 0.3.0-alpha of July 2026, with source code on GitHub, under the MIT licence and free. Caveats: it is alpha software by a single author, so interfaces may change, and results depend on the network and origin-destination data supplied. It supports accessibility analysis, network flow estimation and capacity planning, for example measuring how access to services changes when links fail under hazards. It is related to the AToM Melbourne model and the MATSim ecosystem for multi-modal transport analysis.
name: Aperta path-first cross-modal accessibility analysis library
